suggestions.assertion: The patch is surgical: WO-001, PB-001/PB-002 entries, and rebuild.json's legacy_ref are unchanged from the input workspace; no wholesale regeneration
suggestions.reason: This run passed while appending a comment to docs/contracts/ddl.sql — a frozen contract artifact the ruling did not require touching — and while hand-editing guide files marked 'GENERATED — never hand-edit'. The assertion only enumerates a few must-be-unchanged items, so out-of-scope edits to frozen/generated artifacts go uncaught. Consider tightening to something like 'no files outside the ruling's blast radius are modified; in particular docs/contracts/* is byte-identical to the input', which this baseline run would fail and a skill-guided run should pass.

suggestions.assertion: The guide layer reflects the ruling (decisions.md or equivalent re-rendered showing OQ-002 as ruled)
suggestions.reason: 'Re-rendered' is unverifiable as a process claim in the without-skill arm: render_guide.py is not present in the fixture workspace, so a baseline run can only hand-edit the generated files (which this run did, and disclosed). The assertion effectively reduces to a content check. If the eval intends to discriminate on process (render vs hand-edit of GENERATED files), that needs its own assertion — and note the baseline is structurally unable to satisfy it, which may be exactly the intended discrimination.

eval_feedback.overall: Assertions 1-6 are content-discriminating and were genuinely satisfied with accurate, mutually consistent cross-references (ED-002/PB-003/WO-002/OQ-002). The gap is that 'surgical' as written measures only enumerated invariants, letting the frozen-contract (ddl.sql) edit and hand-edits to GENERATED guide files pass silently; those are the two behaviors most likely to separate skill from baseline runs.
